claims.text: A graph neural network can accurately predict separate lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The graph-neural-network approach will outperform earlier predictive methods.
The graph-neural-network approach captures atomic-scale complexity.
The graph-neural-network approach captures the effects of defects on heat transport.
The applicable material state is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal that may contain defects and impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed intervention is implementation of a graph-neural-network-based predictive model.
The model is intended to apply below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
Atomic-scale structure and defect configuration are the structural features mediating the prediction.
Machine-learning regression is the mechanism used to predict transport properties.
The proposed method may reduce prediction error by 20–30% relative to earlier approaches.
Measured total thermal conductivity from 300 to 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K m).
Model accuracy may decrease below 200 K and above 1200 K because of insufficient training data or physical limitations.
Predictions are especially uncertain below 50 K and above 1500 K because experimental data are limited.
The model should be tested by comparing predicted lattice, electronic, and total thermal conductivities with measurements below 200 K and above 1000 K.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted lattice and electronic contributions deviate from experimental measurements by more than 30% at multiple temperatures.

contradictions.description: The conditions identify temperatures below 200 K as an intended application range, while the boundary simultaneously describes the entire range below 200 K as one where model accuracy may decrease. The usable low-temperature domain is therefore not clearly defined.
